docs.title: Delaunay-Watershed 3D
docs.text:
Delaunay-Watershed-3D (package dw3d) reconstructs, from a 3-D instance segmentation of cells or nuclei, a multimaterial surface mesh: one triangle mesh of every interface between two cells, or between a cell and the medium. It is the reconstruction behind foambryo, which infers surface tensions and cell pressures from these meshes.

  • Getting started: installation, the input, the output, a first mesh.
  • User guide: reconstruction variants, junction relocation, cropped tissues, anisotropic voxels, the .rec metadata appendix.
  • Examples: the notebooks.
  • API reference, generated from the docstrings.
  • Changelog and release notes.

If you use it, please cite: Ichbiah S., Delbary F., McDougall A., Dumollard R., Turlier H. Embryo mechanics cartography: inference of 3D force atlases from fluorescence microscopy. Nature Methods 20(12), 1989–1999 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41592-023-02084-7.

Delaunay-Watershed is free software, under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version (GPL-3.0-or-later).

docs.title: 0.7.0 — 2026-10-17
docs.text:
0.6.0 was prepared (4 October 2026) but not published on PyPI: its changes are part of 0.7.0, listed at the end of this section under "Prepared for 0.6.0". 0.7.0 is the first release on PyPI since 0.5.1.

Recent work on dw3d and foambryo is part of a collaboration with Alejandro Aguilera Castrejon (Janelia Research Campus, Howard Hughes Medical Institute). We thank him and his Janelia colleagues Adam L. Taylor, Wenhong Li and Francesco Roncato. Adam L. Taylor found the border-triangle winding defect fixed in 0.6.0 and pointed us to the seed-extraction and dense tension-solve bottlenecks on large tissues.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.text:
• The README is shorter and points to a user guide in docs/ (reconstruction variants, junction relocation, cropped tissues, anisotropic voxels, the .rec metadata appendix), from which a documentation website is built with MkDocs (mkdocs.yml), with an API reference generated from the docstrings. A new notebook, example_6_anisotropic_voxels_and_crop_faces.ipynb, runs on a mask it generates. The notebooks no longer contain install cells (they say what to install), and the first notebook says that data/Images/1.tif records no voxel size, so the sizes it uses are illustrative. The docstrings of the public functions were checked against the code. No mesh changes.
  • Two return annotations corrected: both_construct_mesh_and_compressed_segmentation returns four items (the mesh's three arrays and the compressed-segmentation dictionary), and reconstruct_mask_from_dict and reconstruct_mask_from_saved_file_dict return 64-bit integer labels, not uint8. What they return is unchanged.

docs.title: Fixed (changes results)
docs.text: • set_pixel_size now scales the right axes; results change when the xy and z sizes differ. dw3d's mesh points are in the mask's index order, (z, y, x) for a microscope stack, so column 0 is z. dw3d.mesh_utilities.set_pixel_size(points, xy_pixel_size, z_pixel_size), the method algorithm.set_pixel_size(xy_pixel_size, z_pixel_size) and dw3d.set_points_pixel_size now scale column 0 by the z size and columns 1 and 2 by the xy size. Before, they scaled columns 0 and 1 by the xy size and column 2 by the z size: z was multiplied by the xy size and x by the z size. Results change only when the two sizes differ; re-run any analysis that called one of them with different sizes. (A mask stored as (x, y, z) was scaled correctly before and is not now: transpose it to (z, y, x) before meshing.) For a mask whose voxels are longer along z, prefer algorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing), which resamples the mask to cubic voxels before meshing: measured on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells voxelised at a real cell size and down-sampled along z, against the same tissues meshed at full resolution, it costs +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17 degrees of contact-angle error at z/xy ratios of 5/3, 2 and 3, against +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 for meshing the native grid and scaling the mesh.

docs.title: Faster
docs.text: • The distance transform needs less memory and the tesselation graph is built faster; the meshes are bit for bit the same. The distance transform builds its masks in uint8 and its field in float32 (still returned as float64), and the tesselation graph pairs the faces of the tetrahedra and builds its networkx graph without Python loops. Measured on one machine, on a 1 866-cell tissue: the distance transform's peak memory goes from 21.0 to 14.9 GiB (38.1 to 28.1 GiB when the mask is first resampled to cubic voxels), the face table and pairing from 7.8 to 1.8 s, the graph from 5.5 to 3.0 s; on a 2 000-cell synthetic foam the whole reconstruction goes from 200 to 186 s. The meshes, crop faces and cut cells of 481 masks (benchmark, resolution sweep, simulated tissues at real cell size, cut and anisotropic masks) and of two large tissues are bitwise identical before and after. Contributed by Wenhong Li and Adam L. Taylor.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• dw3d.io.load_rec_appendix reads resampled_spacing as a number. It returned the text ('0.3'); it now returns a float (0.3), as it already did for spacing. resampling stays text.
  • dw3d.viewing.plot_cells_polyscope(..., anisotropy_factor=...) no longer rescales the reconstruction's mesh. With a factor other than 1 it multiplied column 0 of the algorithm's own points in place, so every call compounded the factor and a later save_to_rec_mesh or save_to_vtk_mesh wrote the scaled points. It now shows a scaled copy and leaves the mesh as it was. If you saved a mesh after viewing it with a factor, reconstruct and save it again. To mesh a mask whose voxels are longer along z in physical units, use algorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing).
  • A reconstruction no longer prints a SciPy DeprecationWarning. The seed lookup imported the k-d tree from scipy.spatial.ckdtree, a namespace SciPy will remove in 2.0; it now uses scipy.spatial.cKDTree, the same class, so the meshes are unchanged.
  • dw3d.io.load_meshio_mesh refuses a file without labels with a ValueError. A file with no label1 or label2 triangle cell array raised meshio's KeyError; it now raises the ValueError the function already raised for empty label arrays, naming the file and the missing array. load_meshio_mesh_with_crop_faces likewise. If you caught KeyError there, catch ValueError.
  • A binary .rec file always reads back. save_rec(..., binary_mode=True) wrote the points in their own dtype, while load_rec reads float64, so float32 points did not read back; they are now always written as float64. For float64 points, which is what dw3d produces, the files are byte for byte what they were. The text layout is unchanged. Both layouts are now described in save_rec's docstring and in the user guide's page on the .rec format.
  • The compressed segmentation after construct_mesh_in_physical_units says which frame each entry is in. algorithm.last_compressed_segmentation returns the mesh's points, which that method has scaled to physical units, with the seeds and the shape of the resampled cubic grid that was meshed. Passed as they are to dw3d.reconstruct_mask_from_dict, the mesh is rasterised at the wrong scale; divide the points by the resampled spacing (the shortest spacing) first, and the resampled mask is rebuilt. The docstrings now say so; nothing returned has changed.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• New: masks with voxels longer along z. algorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing=(0.5, 0.3, 0.3)) resamples the mask to cubic voxels of the shortest spacing by shape-based interpolation, meshes it, and returns the mesh in the unit of spacing; save_to_rec_mesh then records coordinate_frame = physical, the mask's own spacing, source_shape, resampling and resampled_spacing in the file's metadata appendix. The resampling alone is dw3d.resample_to_isotropic(mask, spacing, method="shape"). Meshing the native grid and scaling the mesh, as before, samples the surfaces coarsely along z: measured on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells voxelised at a real cell size and down-sampled along z (one seed), as the median over tissues of each mesh's median line-mean contact-angle error minus that of the same tissue meshed at full resolution, it costs +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 degrees at z/xy ratios of 5/3, 2 and 3, against +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17 when the mask is resampled first. Nothing was measured above a ratio of 3: there the method warns (dw3d.UnmeasuredAnisotropyWarning) and still meshes. The cost is that of a mask acquired at the finer spacing (time and memory grow with the ratio). Nothing changes for construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, its meshes or its files, and a mask with cubic voxels goes through resample_to_isotropic untouched.
  • New: the reconstruction records where the image cut the tissue. When a cell of the mask reaches a face of the image box, the triangles that close it on that face are not contact with the medium: the tissue goes on beyond the image. The algorithm now marks them as crop faces (algorithm.crop_faces, a boolean per triangle) and the cells they touch as cut cells (algorithm.cut_cells); algorithm.crop_face_report gives the counts per image face. The mesh itself is unchanged, bit for bit: same points, same triangles in the same order, same labels. foambryo reads these marks and keeps crop faces out of its equations.
  • New: an image face can be declared physical, for a tissue that really ends there, such as on a coverslip: algorithm.physical_image_faces = ("axis0_low",) before reconstructing, or MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory().set_physical_image_faces("axis0_low"). The triangles on a physical face stay contact with the medium, as before. By default every image face is a crop.
  • .rec and .vtk files keep the crop. save_to_rec_mesh (and save_rec(..., crop_faces=...)) writes the crop faces as the last block of triangles and records the block in the file's metadata appendix as crop_faces = <first row> <count>, with physical_image_faces; dw3d.io.load_rec_with_crop_faces reads them back. save_to_vtk_mesh adds a crop_face cell array, read by load_meshio_mesh_with_crop_faces. Only meshes of masks whose cells reach the image box are affected: for every other mesh the files are byte for byte what they were. A program that does not know the new key still reads a valid mesh, in which the crop faces look like medium contact.
  • Measured on the 47 benchmark masks cut by planes at 10 %, 25 % and 40 % of their extent: read as contact with the medium, crop faces put 13 % to 40 % error on the tensions foambryo infers for the interfaces that touch the crop, against 9 % to 12 % when they are kept out.
  • A reconstruction can also close a cell on an image face that the mask's cell does not reach, when the mask leaves only a voxel or two of medium between the cell and the image border. Those triangles are not crop faces: the cell was seen to end inside the image, so they stay contact with the medium, as before. A mask none of whose cells reaches the image box therefore has no crop face and no cut cell. algorithm.crop_face_report counts them, and lists which cells reach each image face.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• The three reconstruction getters deprecated since 0.5.0 are removed, with their top-level aliases. Each was an exact synonym of a keyword call on get_junction_protected_algorithm (top level: get_junction_protected_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm), which gives the same mesh, bit for bit; call that instead:
  • get_offset_included_algorithm(...) → get_junction_protected_algorithm(...);
  • get_offset_excluded_algorithm(...) → get_junction_protected_algorithm(..., exclude_offsets_from_surface=True);
  • get_cubic_score_algorithm(...) → get_junction_protected_algorithm(..., spline_order=3).

docs.title: Dependencies
docs.text: • Higher minimum versions, the oldest with which the test suite passes (Python 3.11): numpy 2.0.0, scipy 1.13.0, scikit-image 0.23.1, edt 2.4.1 and meshio 5.3.5 (trimesh 4.0.0 and networkx 2.8.0 unchanged); for the viewing extra polyscope 2.2.0 and matplotlib 3.8.4. The previous minimums had never been tested: with them (numpy 1.24) the reconstruction gives slightly different meshes and the rebuilt mask 32-bit labels, and edt 2.4.0, meshio 5.3.4 and older scipy and scikit-image releases do not work with numpy 2.

docs.title: Prepared for 0.6.0 (4 October 2026, not published)
docs.text:
• Faster, and lighter in memory, on large tissues; the meshes are bit-for-bit the same. Three steps of the reconstruction were rewritten without changing any result:
  • the seeds are found in two passes over the volume instead of one pass per label;
  • junction relocation's self-intersection guard finds its candidate vertex pairs with one batched neighbour search per range of reach, and checks only the triangles those pairs involve;
  • the trijunction curves are detected in slabs of the volume instead of on the whole volume at once.

Measured on one machine on a 1 866-cell tissue meshed on its native grid, together with foambryo's sparse tension solve: from mask to tensions, 9.5 min instead of 47.5 min with 0.5.1, and a peak memory of 30.9 GiB instead of 54.7 GiB (measured again for 0.7.0, nothing else running). Seed extraction went from 28 min to 6 s, the relocation guard from 6.6 min to 45 s, and curve detection from 82 s to 49 s and from 37.6 to 9.7 GiB. The meshes of the 47 benchmark masks, 492 embryo timepoints, 10 cut masks and the 4 example images are bitwise identical before and after, as are those of two large tissues. The memory peak is now junction relocation's whole-mesh self-intersection check.

  • New: the cells whose mesh volume disagrees with their mask are listed, with one warning. A reconstruction can lose a small cell, or give part of a cell to a neighbour, while the mesh stays closed and manifold, so no surface check sees it. After every reconstruction the algorithm now compares each cell's mesh volume with its voxel count and lists, in cell_volume_report, the cells outside 0.5–1.5 times it, with a non-positive volume, or with no surface at all; CellVolumeDisagreementWarning is emitted once when the list is not empty. The same check is available as dw3d.compare_cell_volumes_with_mask. The mesh itself is unchanged, bit for bit. Measured with the default settings: 2 of 240 cells on the 47 benchmark masks, 169 of 5 038 on two 246-timepoint embryo series (almost all in the last frames of one series, where the mask suddenly holds many very small labels), 20 cells and 45 cavities on a 1 866-cell tissue. Interfaces of the listed cells are missing or misplaced, and a pressure inferred for them is not a measurement.

  • The repository no longer ships lock files. uv.lock recorded version 0.4.1 and a package index that only the lab can reach, and locked-requirements.txt pinned version 0.3.5. The supported dependency ranges are those in pyproject.toml.

  • The package metadata names the Turlier lab as author; Matthieu Perez remains the maintainer.

  • Fixed: triangles on the image border were wound the wrong way. When a cell touches the edge of the image, the triangles that close it along the image border had their normal pointing out of the cell instead of into it, against the convention every other triangle follows (the normal points from the first label into the second). Every such triangle was affected, not a random share. A cell closed by the image border then reads too small a volume, often a negative one, and any tension or pressure computed from the mesh is wrong.

Who is affected. Anyone whose cells touch the image border, above all tissue cropped through its cells. Measured with the default reconstruction on ten benchmark masks cut through their middle: before the fix, 38 of the 54 cells on the cut had a negative volume; after it, none. The tensions foambryo infers from those meshes changed by up to 199 %, and every cell pressure by 37–139 %. On masks whose cells stay clear of the border nothing changes: of 543 uncut masks (47 benchmark cases, 492 embryo timepoints and the 4 example images), 542 have no border triangle and come out bit-for-bit identical. The one exception has two border triangles on a single cell, whose volume goes from 0.73 to 1.01 of its voxel count.

Only the vertex order of border triangles changes: vertex positions, the set of triangles and their labels are identical. A cut surface is still treated as contact with the medium, as before.

  • Fixed: a few triangles lying on a flat tetrahedron were wound the wrong way. The tetrahedral mesh the surface is cut from contains flat tetrahedra (four coplanar points of the voxel grid). A triangle whose orientation was read from such a tetrahedron got its winding from a rounding error, and about half of them came out reversed; each reversed triangle makes its two cells read a volume slightly different from the volume they actually enclose. These triangles are now oriented from the tetrahedron on their other side. Measured with the default settings: 10 triangles in 8 cells on the 47 benchmark masks (volume error 0.4 % median, 0.7 % at most), 20 triangles in 19 cells on two 246-timepoint embryo series (2 % median, 14 % at most), 9 triangles in 10 cells on a 1 866-cell tissue; after the fix, every cell's volume equals that of the tetrahedra it is made of. Only the vertex order of those triangles changes: vertex positions, the set of triangles and their labels are bit-for-bit identical on every mask measured.

  • Fixed: junction relocation could turn a very small cell inside out. Relocation's guard checked that every triangle around a moved vertex kept its orientation, but a cell made of a single tetrahedron could still be inverted by a vertex moved across its opposite face, with every triangle around it passing that check; the cell then had a negative volume and passed every surface check. The guard now also refuses a move that would leave any cell it touches with a volume of zero or less, and nothing else: a cell may still shrink. A refused move leaves its vertex where it was; relocation_report counts these refusals and names the cells. Measured with the default settings: the clause changes no mesh of the 47 benchmark masks, the 141 masks of the resolution sweep, 10 masks cut through their cells, a 110-cell tissue, or 484 timepoints of two embryo series (all bit-for-bit identical). It fires on two over-segmented frames of an embryo series, where it keeps one cell from inverting on one frame, and on a 1 866-cell tissue, where it keeps one cavity from inverting.

0.5.1 republishes the final 0.5.0 (as on GitHub's master since 27 September). The 0.5.0 wheel and source archive on PyPI were built from an earlier snapshot of the release: their licence metadata says CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 instead of GPL-3.0-or-later, the viewing extra still installs napari, and dw3d.viewing still has the napari viewer that 0.5.0 removed. GitHub's v0.5.0 tag points at that same earlier snapshot, and is left as it is. Install 0.5.1; 0.5.0 is withdrawn from PyPI (yanked).

Nothing else changes: the code is the final 0.5.0's. The package metadata names the Turlier lab as author (Matthieu Perez remains the maintainer), the README's links point to the 0.5.1 tag, and the two stale lock files 0.5.0 carried (uv.lock and locked-requirements.txt) are gone.

New licence: from 0.5.0, delaunay-watershed-3d is licensed under the GNU General Public License, version 3 or (at your option) any later version (SPDX GPL-3.0-or-later; the text of version 3 is in License), replacing CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Commercial use is allowed, under the GPL's conditions (a distributed derivative work must be released under the same licence, with its source). Earlier releases keep the licence they were published under.

The default changed: junction relocation is on in every reconstruction configuration. Meshes come out with the same triangles and labels as in 0.4, and different vertex positions on the trijunction lines. To get the 0.4 meshes back exactly, switch it off: pass relocate_junctions=False to MeshReconstructionAlgorithm, call MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory().set_junction_relocation(False), or set algorithm.relocate_junctions = False on an algorithm a get_*_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm function returned. See RELEASE_NOTES.md for the limitations that matter on real data.

  • Junction relocation, now the default. dw3d.relocate_junction_vertices is a post-process on a finished mesh that moves its trijunction vertices onto the trijunction curves the mask itself gives. It changes vertex positions only — triangles and material labels come back untouched — so a treated mesh can be compared vertex-for-vertex with its own untreated original. Read what it did from the algorithm's relocation_report, and whether it ran, with which guard and whether it warned from the new relocation_provenance.

What it costs, in seconds, because the reconstruction it follows varies by an order of magnitude between volumes: about +0.75 s on the benchmark meshes, whose reconstruction takes about 5 s (+15 %); 0.1–1.5 s per timepoint on real embryo volumes, whose reconstruction takes about 0.6 s (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on two developmental time series; about 65 s per 154-timepoint series). Within one real series it grows faster than linearly with the number of triangles — a fitted exponent of 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range of mesh sizes, which describes that series and is not a tissue-scale law. A faster neighbour search is planned for 0.5.1; it will leave every relocated mesh bit-for-bit unchanged.

  • New warning: dw3d.CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning (a UserWarning), emitted once per reconstruction when relocation is on and the point placement's min_distance is 5 or more. Its text: "At min_distance ≥ 5, the check on surface-tangent contact angles showed a small drift that lies within the check's own noise, and larger spacings have not been measured; facet-based contact angles improve. If tangent-based angles matter for your analysis, compare with relocate_junctions=False (or set_junction_relocation(False))." A custom point-placement function that carries no min_distance never triggers it. Filter it like any warning: warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=dw3d.CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning).

  • Removed, as their deprecation warnings announced since 0.4.0: get_v0_3_algorithm (use get_dithered_algorithm), get_a1b_algorithm (use get_deterministic_algorithm), get_a3_a5_algorithm (use get_junction_protected_algorithm), and the matching top-level get_v0_3_…, get_a1b_… and get_a3_a5_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm.

  • Removed, without a deprecation period: dw3d.viewing.plot_in_napari. It already failed with the napari that pip installs today: with napari 0.9.1 (measured on 27 Sep 2026) it raised AttributeError, because napari.view_image no longer exists, and its add_points calls pass an n_dimensional argument that napari 0.9.1 no longer accepts. napari is no longer part of the viewing extra, which now installs Polyscope and matplotlib only; the Polyscope viewer dw3d.viewing.plot_cells_polyscope is unchanged.

  • Deprecated, removed in 0.6.0 — three exact synonyms, which now emit a DeprecationWarning naming the equivalent call and still return the identical mesh: get_offset_included_algorithm() → get_junction_protected_algorithm(); get_offset_excluded_algorithm(...) → get_junction_protected_algorithm(..., exclude_offsets_from_surface=True); get_cubic_score_algorithm() → get_junction_protected_algorithm(spline_order=3); and their top-level get_*_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm aliases. Six configurations remain recommended: default, dithered, deterministic, link-checked, junction-protected and boundary-layer.

  • Golden masters. tests/golden/ now holds the relocated meshes; the 0.4 fixtures moved, byte for byte, to tests/golden_without_relocation/, and every golden-master test runs against both — the second with relocate_junctions=False.

  • Documentation. BENCHMARKS.md is self-contained: each number states its population and how it was measured. Those numbers were measured without junction relocation (the 0.4 default). Docstrings no longer cite files that are not distributed. The README cites the published article (Ichbiah et al., Nature Methods 2023, doi:10.1038/s41592-023-02084-7) instead of its preprint, and a new CITATION.cff says the same. The mask-compression notebook (Examples/example_2_mask_compression_reconstruction.ipynb) opens its napari viewer with napari.Viewer() and add_image, since napari.view_image no longer exists in current napari, and says that napari must be installed separately; the advanced-use notebook (example_3_advanced_use.ipynb) no longer has its napari section.

The rest of this section describes what 0.5.0 adds besides the default:

What it costs and what it buys, measured over 40 benchmark cases at four reconstruction spacings and on four point samplers — 16 independent adjudications, all passing. Line position error, local tangent error and discrete curvature all improve with their confidence intervals clear of zero at every spacing on every sampler; no pre-existing mesh-validity number changes on any case. On the seed-free samplers it also improves contact angles by 2.3–3.5 degrees and gauge-matched tension error by 20–40 %; on the shipped default's seeded sampler the line improves and the contact angle does not move significantly either way. Its cost is stated in seconds above.

It is guarded twice. The local guard refuses any move that would invert or collapse a triangle touching the vertex. The second guard is the one that matters: a move can drive one sheet of the mesh through a distant sheet while every triangle around the moved vertex stays perfectly oriented, and no local check can see that. Measured on the benchmark cohort, all twelve existing validity numbers stayed bit-identical on 40 of 40 cases while 23 such crossings existed on 5 of them. The second guard makes the crossing count non-increasing by construction, and it costs between 0.04 % and 0.21 % of the moves to do it.

  • dw3d.find_self_intersections and dw3d.count_self_intersections. The exact triangle–triangle intersection test the relocation certifies itself with, now part of the library. Two triangles sharing a vertex are adjacent and are never tested — three triangles meet along every trijunction edge by design — so what it counts is a genuine defect, never the intended non-manifold structure. It is a count, never a score, and no threshold is proposed.

No change to reconstruction behaviour: every default is bitwise identical to 0.4.1 (verified by hash on the mesh output of the dithered and deterministic configurations).

  • The three deprecation warnings' text no longer implies 0.5.0 already exists. get_v0_3_algorithm, get_a1b_algorithm and get_a3_a5_algorithm (and the matching dw3d/__init__.py aliases) now say "removed in a future 0.5.0 release" instead of "removed in 0.5.0"; the replacement function and the removal commitment are unchanged.
  • New dw3d_benchmarks/mesh_quality_comparison/ package: compares mesh quality (M1-M7: contact angles, interface areas, cell volumes, curvature, junction-line geometry, mesh validity, cost) across the four core reconstruction configurations and across dw3d versions. A benchmarks extra (pip install ".[benchmarks]") covers the figure scripts' matplotlib requirement without pulling in viewing's napari dependency.
  • One-line fix: dw3d_benchmarks/run_case.py's VARIANT_GETTERS comment stated the default is offset_excluded_linkcheck; it is not — the default is dithered.

Release hygiene only. No change to reconstruction behaviour: every default is bitwise identical to 0.4.0 on all 47 benchmark meshes.

  • MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory's three development-named factory methods are renamed to describe their mechanism: get_v0_3_algorithm → get_dithered_algorithm, get_a1b_algorithm → get_deterministic_algorithm, get_a3_a5_algorithm → get_offset_included_algorithm, and the matching top-level exports in dw3d/__init__.py (e.g. get_v0_3_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm → get_dithered_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm). The old names still work — they now emit a DeprecationWarning naming the replacement — and will be removed in 0.5.0.
  • dw3d_benchmarks/run_fingerprints.py's --variant strings are renamed to match (v0_3 → dithered, a1b → deterministic, a3_a5 → offset_included); the old strings are still accepted, with a printed note pointing at the replacement.
  • Development files no longer ship or return. Development notes and scratch scripts are removed from the repository tip and gitignored so they cannot be re-added by accident. The project's development record is kept in the development repository and has never been part of the packaged distribution; confirmed by building the wheel and listing its contents.
  • Internal benchmark filenames and test names that were named after a development phase (e.g. analyze_a5.py, d2_defect_patches.py, baseline JSONs prefixed a6_/a7_/a8_/a8b_) are renamed to describe what they measure. This does not change any benchmark's recorded numbers.

docs.title: New: trijunction curves read from the mask, keyed to the mesh's own junctions
docs.text:
extract_junction_curves(mask, points, triangles, labels) returns one polyline per material triple, computed from the segmentation mask and matched against the reconstructed mesh's own trijunctions. Purely additive: nothing in the reconstruction pipeline calls it, no default changed, no dependency was added, and the contact-angle and mesh-validity numbers are bitwise unchanged (verified on 1974 measured values across 47 cases at two point spacings).

from dw3d import extract_junction_curves
from dw3d.io import load_rec

points, triangles, labels = load_rec("000_mesh.rec")  # or your own reconstruction
curves = extract_junction_curves(mask, points, triangles, labels)
curves.matched      # the usable set: one-to-one with a mesh trijunction
curves.invented     # triples the mask says exist and the mesh does not have
curves.match_rate   # 0.900 on the 47-case benchmark at min_distance=3

Why you might want it. These curves are measurably closer to ground truth than the junction lines the mesh produces on its own — median position error 0.5846 voxels against 0.8642 at min_distance=3, a factor of 1.48, and more as the mesh coarsens (1.90x at min_distance=7). Every head-to-head comparison measured favours them on 1.000 of 10,000 bootstrap draws.

What it costs you. They are less complete: 90 % of the mesh's trijunctions get exactly one curve, and the rest arrive fragmented. matched and invented are deliberately separate fields and are never merged, because they are structurally different populations — matched curves lie a median 0.68 voxels from all three of their own interfaces, invented ones 29.7, with none within a voxel.

What it is not. The curves sit about 4.8x above the mask's own identifiability floor (0.107 voxels). This is better geometry, not correct geometry.

The default estimator is "plain" — detection only, about 0.8 s per benchmark case against the ~1.5 s dw3d spends reconstructing it. estimator="anchor" solves one small linear program per vertex, costs about six times as much, and buys 11 % of position error; its argument is that it carries a smaller systematic bias against narrow junction wedges, not that 11 %. estimator="centroid" exists to reproduce the research result and is not a recommendation.

See BENCHMARKS.md (section "Junction curves") for the full numbers and the controls, and Examples/example_4_junction_curves.ipynb for a worked example that runs in a few seconds on data already in this repository.

docs.title: The default reconstruction is the published dithered algorithm again
docs.text:
Between one earlier internal release and this one, the default reconstruction algorithm was a revised meshing pipeline (deterministic point placement, explicit junction detection and protection, and a topology-preserving cleanup of the extracted surface). That pipeline produces measurably better mesh geometry — lower interface-area bias against ground truth, far fewer degenerate ("all-surface") tetrahedra, better junction placement — but end-to-end tension-inference accuracy through foambryo, on a benchmark of 42 mechanically-equilibrated cases, is worse with it than with the published algorithm, on every inference method tested. Since that downstream accuracy is what most users of this package ultimately care about, the default reconstruction algorithm has reverted to the published (dithered) configuration.

The revised meshing pipeline is not removed: it remains fully available, opt-in, as get_link_checked_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm. Reach for it when mesh geometry and topology matter more to you than today's downstream inference accuracy. See BENCHMARKS.md for the numbers behind this decision and the accuracy finding stated plainly, without spin: the revised pipeline is currently the worse choice for tension inference, despite being the better mesh in isolation.

This reconstructs bit-for-bit what dw3d 0.3.6 produced on the current numpy/scipy/ scikit-image stack (see get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm's docstring for the one caveat: the pre-0.4.0 watershed tie-break ordering, which had no single well-defined answer, is not restored, since it depended on which sorting kernel happened to run it).

docs.title: New capability, unaffected by the default change
docs.text: • set_tiled_edt_method(..., dtype=np.float64): an opt-in Euclidean-distance-transform variant that uses roughly a third of the peak memory of the default EDT computation at large volumes, while reproducing it bit-for-bit — unlike the existing float32 tiled variant, which saves the same memory but changes the output when combined with the revised meshing pipeline's normal/score computations. Not the default EDT for either reconstruction variant; a deliberate choice for memory-constrained large volumes.

docs.title: .rec / .arec files can now carry a metadata appendix
docs.text:
save_rec(..., metadata={...}) appends a trailing block of ASCII # key = value lines recording coordinate_frame (voxel_index, physical, or unknown — the field this exists for: it is what lets a reader tell whether coordinates are raw voxel indices or already-scaled physical units), axis_order, spacing, spacing_unit, source_shape and crop_offset. Read it back with the new load_rec_appendix(filename), which returns None for a file with no appendix — never a default of isotropic spacing. See README.md for the field list and the format.

The block is written at the end of the file, never the start, so this is purely additive: save_rec without metadata (the default) writes byte-for-byte the same file as before this existed, and every reader already in the wild — including dw3d 0.3.6 and released foambryo — loads a file with an appendix exactly as it always has. load_rec's return type is unchanged; the appendix is read separately, on purpose.

docs.title: Nothing else changed
docs.text: Every other named reconstruction getter (get_deterministic_algorithm, get_offset_included_algorithm, get_boundary_layer_algorithm, get_offset_excluded_algorithm, get_cubic_score_algorithm) is unchanged and produces exactly the output it always has.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Delaunay-Watershed needs Python 3.11 or later:

pip install delaunay-watershed-3d               # the library
pip install "delaunay-watershed-3d[viewing]"    # and the Polyscope viewer

docs.title: The input and the output
docs.text:
The input is a 3-D array of non-negative integer labels: one label per cell (or nucleus), 0 for the medium. Axis 0 is z, axes 1 and 2 are y and x. The output is three arrays:

  • points, (n_points, 3): the vertices, in the mask's (z, y, x) order, in voxels, or in the unit of the spacing with construct_mesh_in_physical_units;
  • triangles, (n_triangles, 3): indices into points;
  • labels, (n_triangles, 2): the two materials on each side of each triangle; the triangle's normal (right-hand rule) points from the first label into the second.

docs.title: A first mesh
docs.text:
import tifffile
from dw3d import get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm

mask = tifffile.imread("segmentation.tif")
algorithm = get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm()          # min_distance=3, junction relocation on
points, triangles, labels = algorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing=(1.0, 0.5, 0.5), spacing_unit="um")
algorithm.save_to_rec_mesh("mesh.rec")
print(algorithm.cut_cells, algorithm.cell_volume_report)

Without a voxel size, construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask) meshes the voxel grid and returns the mesh in voxel units. min_distance is the minimum distance between the tessellation's points, in (cubic) voxels: smaller gives a finer, slower mesh.

To look at it (needs a display): from dw3d.viewing import plot_cells_polyscope; plot_cells_polyscope(algorithm).

docs.title: Release notes — 0.7.0, 17 October 2026
docs.text: delaunay-watershed-3d (this repository) and foambryo ship together as 0.7.0, the first release on PyPI since 0.5.1. 0.6.0 was prepared but not published; its changes are part of 0.7.0 and are included below. This is what changes for you and what can mislead you; CHANGELOG.md has the full list, and foambryo's RELEASE_NOTES.md covers the inference side. Install with pip install --upgrade delaunay-watershed-3d foambryo.

docs.title: What changes for you
docs.text:
1. set_pixel_size scaled the wrong axes; results change when the xy and z sizes differ. dw3d's mesh points are in the mask's index order, (z, y, x) for a microscope stack, so column 0 is z. set_pixel_size (the function in dw3d.mesh_utilities, the reconstruction method and dw3d.set_points_pixel_size) now scales column 0 by the z size and columns 1 and 2 by the xy size. Before, z was multiplied by the xy size and x by the z size. Re-run any analysis that called it with different xy and z sizes; with equal sizes nothing changes. A mask stored as (x, y, z) was scaled correctly before and is not now: transpose it to (z, y, x) before meshing.
  2. Meshes of cells that touch the image border change, and were wrong before. The triangles that close a cell along the image border were wound the wrong way, so such a cell read too small a volume, often a negative one, and any tension or pressure computed from its mesh was wrong. On ten benchmark masks cut through their middle, 38 of the 54 cells on the cut had a negative volume before the fix and none after; the tensions foambryo infers from those meshes changed by up to 199 %, and every cell pressure by 37–139 %. Reconstruct again any mesh whose cells touch the image border, above all tissue cropped through its cells. Only the vertex order of the border triangles changes, and meshes whose cells stay clear of the border are unchanged (542 of 543 uncut masks bit-for-bit; the exception has two border triangles on one cell).
  3. A few triangles lying on flat tetrahedra change orientation (10 triangles in 8 cells on the 47 benchmark masks), so that every cell's volume now equals that of the tetrahedra it is made of.
  4. Junction relocation can no longer turn a very small cell inside out. Its guard now also refuses a move that would leave a cell it touches with a volume of zero or less; relocation_report counts these refusals and names the cells. No mesh of the 47 benchmark masks, the resolution sweep, the cut masks or 484 embryo timepoints changes.
  5. New warning, CellVolumeDisagreementWarning. After every reconstruction, the cells whose mesh volume is outside 0.5–1.5 times their voxel count, non-positive, or missing are listed in cell_volume_report. The interfaces of a listed cell are missing or misplaced, and a pressure inferred for it is not a measurement. Expect it on masks that hold many very small labels.
  6. Faster on large tissues, with the same meshes. Seed extraction, the relocation guard and the trijunction-curve detection were rewritten; every mesh measured is bit-for-bit identical. On a 1 866-cell tissue meshed on its native grid, from mask to tensions with foambryo's sparse tension solve: 9.5 min instead of 47.5 min with 0.5.1, and a peak memory of 30.9 GiB instead of 54.7 GiB (one machine, nothing else running). The peak is now relocation's whole-mesh self-intersection check. The same tissue resampled to cubic voxels first (construct_mesh_in_physical_units) costs more: its reconstruction takes about 13.5 min and 38 GiB.
  7. No lock files. uv.lock and locked-requirements.txt are gone; the supported dependency ranges are those in pyproject.toml.
  8. Viewing a mesh no longer rescales it. plot_cells_polyscope(..., anisotropy_factor=...) with a factor other than 1 multiplied the reconstruction's own z column, so a mesh saved after viewing was scaled: reconstruct and save it again. Also: load_meshio_mesh refuses a file without labels with a ValueError (it raised KeyError), a binary .rec file always stores its points as float64, and a reconstruction no longer prints a SciPy deprecation warning. Reconstructions are unchanged, bit for bit (CHANGELOG.md).
  9. Three deprecated names are removed. get_offset_included_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm, get_offset_excluded_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm and get_cubic_score_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm (and the factory's methods of the same names), deprecated since 0.5.0, are gone. Call get_junction_protected_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm(), the same with exclude_offsets_from_surface=True, or the same with spline_order=3: the meshes are identical, bit for bit.
  10. Higher minimum versions: numpy 2.0.0, scipy 1.13.0, scikit-image 0.23.1, edt 2.4.1, meshio 5.3.5 (polyscope 2.2.0 and matplotlib 3.8.4 for viewing), the oldest with which the test suite passes. Older numpy releases give slightly different meshes.

docs.title: New
docs.text:
• Masks with voxels longer along z: algorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing) resamples the mask to cubic voxels of the shortest spacing by shape-based interpolation, meshes it, and returns the mesh in the unit of spacing; save_to_rec_mesh records the frame, the spacing and the resampling. Measured on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells voxelised at a real cell size and down-sampled along z, against the same tissues meshed at full resolution: +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17 degrees of contact-angle error at z/xy ratios of 5/3, 2 and 3, against +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 for meshing the native grid and scaling the mesh.
  • Crop faces and cut cells: algorithm.crop_faces, algorithm.cut_cells, algorithm.crop_face_report, physical_image_faces; .rec and .vtk files keep them. The mesh is unchanged, bit for bit.
  • A lighter distance transform and a faster tesselation graph; the meshes are bit for bit the same. The distance transform builds its masks in uint8 and its field in float32 (still returned as float64), and the tesselation graph is built without Python loops. Measured on one machine, on a 1 866-cell tissue: the distance transform's peak memory goes from 21.0 to 14.9 GiB (38.1 to 28.1 GiB when the mask is first resampled to cubic voxels), the face table and pairing from 7.8 to 1.8 s, the graph from 5.5 to 3.0 s; on a 2 000-cell synthetic foam the whole reconstruction goes from 200 to 186 s. The meshes, crop faces and cut cells of 481 masks and of two large tissues are bitwise identical before and after. Contributed by Wenhong Li and Adam L. Taylor.

docs.title: What can mislead you
docs.text:
1. Above a z/xy ratio of 3 nothing was measured: UnmeasuredAnisotropyWarning, and the mesh is built anyway.
  2. min_distance counts voxels of the resampled, cubic grid in construct_mesh_in_physical_units: the mesh, its time and its memory are those of a mask acquired at the short spacing, so they grow with the ratio.
  3. A crop face is not contact with the medium. A program that does not read the crop-face key of a .rec file reads a valid mesh in which the crop faces look like medium contact.
  4. The limitations listed for 0.5.0 below still hold, except 7, which concerns foambryo and is fixed in its 0.7.0, and the end of 8: the faster neighbour search planned for 0.5.1 is in 0.7.0 (item 6 above), and on a 1 866-cell tissue the relocation guard takes 45 s instead of 6.6 min, with the same meshes (CHANGELOG.md).

docs.title: The one change that affects every mesh
docs.text:
Junction relocation is on by default, in every reconstruction configuration. After the mesh is built, its trijunction vertices are moved onto the trijunction curves the segmentation mask itself gives, under a guard that cannot create a self-intersection anywhere in the mesh. Triangles and material labels are unchanged; vertex positions on trijunction lines are not. Measured over 40 equilibrium benchmark cases, four spacings and four point samplers: junction-line position, tangent and curvature errors all improve with their confidence intervals clear of zero, and no mesh-validity number changes.

To get the 0.4 meshes back exactly:

algorithm = get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm()
algorithm.relocate_junctions = False

or MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory().set_junction_relocation(False), or MeshReconstructionAlgorithm(..., relocate_junctions=False). Whether relocation ran on your mesh is in algorithm.relocation_provenance.

At min_distance >= 5 you will see CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning, once per reconstruction: at that spacing the check on surface-tangent contact angles showed a small drift within its own noise, and larger spacings are unmeasured; facet-based angles improve. If tangent-based angles matter for your analysis, compare with relocate_junctions=False.

docs.title: Names removed and deprecated
docs.text: Removed: get_v0_3_algorithm, get_a1b_algorithm, get_a3_a5_algorithm (use get_dithered_algorithm, get_deterministic_algorithm, get_junction_protected_algorithm). Removed without a deprecation period: dw3d.viewing.plot_in_napari, which already failed with napari 0.9.1; napari is no longer part of the viewing extra (Polyscope and matplotlib only). Deprecated, removed in 0.6.0: get_offset_included_algorithm, get_offset_excluded_algorithm, get_cubic_score_algorithm — exact synonyms of keyword calls on get_junction_protected_algorithm, which their warnings name.

docs.title: Limitations
docs.text:
Every item is measured; each is one sentence and its number.

  1. The benchmark under-rewards tangent-based improvements. Its ground-truth meshes are facet-equilibrated (Surface Evolver), so an improvement in the surface-tangent description of a contact angle is scored against a facet-based truth and can read as no change.
  2. The second-order angle reader has its own floor, and it cannot resolve junction relocation's effect. On a perfectly smooth analytic surface it reads contact angles with a floor of 0.245°, and at every point spacing measured (0 of 32 spacing-by-variant cells) its check could not resolve the effect of junction relocation on tangent-based angles, in either direction.
  3. On real embryos, do not use second-order line means at sub-degree scale. The second-order reader covers a median 0.804 of incident trijunction faces on real embryo meshes (minimum 0.454), and its line means move by 1.75° [1.41, 2.17] when uncovered faces are excluded instead of filled by the chord reading.
  4. Real embryo cells are small in voxels, so every benchmark statement is about one spacing step optimistic for them. Their equivalent radius at trijunctions is a median 17.6 voxels against 38.2 in the benchmark, so real data at min_distance 3 sits where the benchmark sits at min_distance 4; for cells this small, consider a smaller min_distance.
  5. Folded trijunctions on real meshes are mostly real geometry. Real embryo meshes carry 3.2× the benchmark's fraction of reflex (folded) trijunctional edges, and more than half of them sit where the segmentation mask's own wedge already exceeds 180°.
  6. The force-balance residual rho_free alarms on every reconstructed mesh. Its median is 0.578 on reconstructed meshes against 0.0118 on the reference meshes, so a high value on your mesh is expected and is not by itself a sign of a bad segmentation.
  7. ForceBalanceMAP is not scale-invariant, contrary to its docstring: rescaling a mesh moves its relative tensions by up to 43 %; plain ForceBalance is exact under rescaling.
  8. Junction relocation, now on by default, has a cost that grows faster than linearly with mesh size. It adds about +0.75 s to a ~5 s benchmark reconstruction (+15 %) and 0.1–1.5 s per timepoint to a ~0.6 s real-embryo reconstruction (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on two developmental time series, about 65 s per 154-timepoint series); within one real series it grows with triangle count with a fitted exponent of 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range of mesh sizes, which is not a tissue-scale law. A faster neighbour search is planned for 0.5.1, and will leave every relocated mesh bit-for-bit unchanged.

docs.title: Cell volumes against the mask
docs.text: List the cells whose reconstructed mesh volume disagrees with their voxel count.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text:
A reconstruction can lose a cell or misplace part of it while the mesh stays closed, manifold and free of self-intersections, so no topological check sees it. Measured with the default algorithm at min_distance 3: on the 47 benchmark masks 2 of 240 cells, on two 246-timepoint real embryo series 169 of 5 038, and on a 1 866-cell tissue 20 cells, have a mesh volume below half or above one and a half times their voxel count, a non-positive volume, or no surface at all. Almost all of them are small cells (a few hundred voxels, about two voxels thick) that the seeded watershed never grows out of; one is a single-tetrahedron cell that junction relocation turned inside out. Their interfaces are missing or misplaced, and a pressure inferred for such a cell is not a measurement.

This module changes no geometry. It compares each label's mesh volume with its voxel count and reports the labels that fall outside a fixed range, so that a user, or foambryo, can see which cells to distrust.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text: The mesh volume of a label is the divergence-theorem volume with the package's winding convention: +det(p0, p1, p2) / 6 for every triangle whose first label it is, -det / 6 for every triangle whose second label it is. Volumes are in cubic voxels, so the comparison is made on the mesh in mask voxel units, before any pixel-size scaling. Label 0 is the exterior medium and is never listed. The range [0.5, 1.5] is inclusive; its bounds are fixed, not tuning parameters.

docs.title: Crop faces
docs.text: Which faces of a reconstructed mesh are crop faces, and which cells the crop cuts.

docs.title: The problem
docs.text:
A segmentation mask whose cells touch a face of the image box was cropped: the tissue goes on beyond the image, and nothing beyond it was observed. The reconstruction closes every such cell with triangles lying on the image face, the border triangles: faces of the tesselation's hull, labelled (0, c), with the cell c on one side and nothing on the other. They are not contact with the medium. A tension or a contact angle read on them measures the crop, not the tissue: on plane crops of the benchmark tissues, reading them as medium contact puts 13 % to 40 % error on the tensions of the interfaces that touch the crop (10 % to 40 % of the tissue removed), against 9 % to 12 % when they are kept out of every equation.

So the reconstruction records them. A crop face is a border triangle on an image face that is not declared physical, and that its cell reaches in the mask. A cut cell is a cell with a crop face, or with a vertex on one: its volume and some of its interfaces were not observed, and its pressure is not a measurement.

The reconstruction also closes a cell on the image box where the mask's cell stops short of the image face: with no point in the few voxels of medium between the cell and the face, the tetrahedra that reach the hull there take the cell's label. Such a border triangle is not a crop, since the cell was observed to end inside the image, and it stays contact with the medium, as on a mesh without crop faces. On a mask none of whose cells reaches an image face, no triangle is a crop face and no cell is cut, whatever the reconstruction put on the hull.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• A border triangle is found from the tesselation itself, not from coordinates: its three tesselation vertices form a lone face of the tesselation (a face with one tetrahedron), which lies on the hull, and the hull is the image box (the point placements put the box's eight corners in the point set). Coordinates would miss some: junction relocation moves a few border-triangle vertices off the image face (23 of 500 on one benchmark mask cut at its mid-plane).
  • The image face a border triangle lies on is read from its vertices' coordinates before relocation, in voxel units of the mask: all three have coordinate 0 ("axis<k>_low") or shape[k] - 1 ("axis<k>_high") along the same axis k. A border triangle on no single image face (none was seen) is a crop face whatever is declared physical.
  • A cell reaches an image face when at least one voxel of the mask on that face (index 0 or shape[k] - 1 along axis k) carries its label. The test is per cell and per image face, with no tolerance: a border triangle is a crop face when its cell has any voxel on the image face the triangle lies on, wherever that voxel is on the face. A border triangle on no single image face is a crop face when its cell reaches an image face, not declared physical, on which one of its vertices lies.
  • An image face can be declared physical (physical_image_faces), for example a coverslip the tissue rests on: its border triangles stay contact with the medium, as before this module existed, and are not crop faces. The default declares none, because the medium beyond the image box is never observed.
  • The mesh is not changed: crop faces keep their labels (0, c) and their place in the triangle array. A crop face is a row of a boolean mask beside the labels, never a reserved label: a label for the crop puts four regions around a three-face junction edge wherever the medium reaches the image face, which no reader of three-region junctions accepts.

Limits of the test, which the report lets a caller check: a cell that reaches an image face at one place is cut, and every border triangle it has on that face is a crop face, even one far from the place where it reaches it; and a cell that reaches a crop image face with too few voxels to get a border triangle is not marked cut (CropFaceReport.cells_reaching_a_crop_without_a_crop_face).

On a mask that touches no image face there are no crop faces and no cut cells, and nothing else in the reconstruction depends on this module.

docs.title: Junction curves
docs.text: Trijunction curves read from the label mask and keyed to a reconstructed mesh's own junctions.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
extract_junction_curves returns one polyline per material triple (a, b, c), computed from the segmentation mask, and says for each whether the reconstructed mesh has exactly one trijunction of that same triple. The curves are more accurate than the mesh's own junction lines and less complete than them; both halves are measured, and the API keeps them apart so a caller cannot get one while thinking it got the other.

Nothing in the reconstruction pipeline calls this and no default changes. It is an additional read of the same mask the mesh was built from.

docs.title: Where the criterion comes from
docs.text: A dual-lattice point -- the corner shared by eight voxels -- lies on the junction line of (a, b, c) iff those eight voxels contain all three labels. junctions.junction_strata already computes exactly this predicate (|L| == 3) for point placement; what this module adds is the split by material triple, the attribution of points carrying four or more labels to every triple they contain (which carries a line into its quadruple point rather than stopping a lattice step short), and the reduction of each 26-connected component to one ordered polyline by the minimum spanning tree's diameter path. Label 0 is an ordinary material: the outer medium's contact lines with the cells are genuine trijunctions.

docs.title: The measured advantage, and the measured limitation
docs.text:
These curves were measured against a registered reference mesh on the 47-case synthetic benchmark, reading each variant at its own median junction-edge spacing so that the comparison is not a comparison of reading resolutions. The position error below is the median distance in voxels from a curve's vertices to the reference polyline; lower is better.

dw3d min_distance these curves the mesh's own lines advantage 2 0.5595 0.7862 1.41x 3 0.5855 0.8642 1.48x 4 0.6173 0.9277 1.50x 7 0.6817 1.2942 1.90x

On the 42 equilibrium cases, all 30 paired comparisons -- five values of min_distance times six geometric metrics -- favour the extraction, in a fraction 1.000 of 10,000 case-level bootstrap draws. At min_distance = 3, relative to the value the reference line itself scores when subsampled at the same spacing, the curves read tortuosity at 1.001 (the mesh: 1.034), curvature at 1.013 (1.172) and tangent error at 1.957x (4.529x).

They are better geometry, not correct geometry. The mask's own identifiability floor -- the best any mask-based method can do -- is 0.107 voxels (BENCHMARKS.md, "Junction curves"). These curves sit at 0.5855, a factor of 4.8 above it, and that gap is open.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text: Everything is in mask voxel units. A dual-lattice point (i, j, k) is emitted at (i + 0.5, j + 0.5, k + 0.5), in the frame a reconstructed dw3d mesh's points live in (construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask; not a mesh scaled by set_pixel_size or built by construct_mesh_in_physical_units). extract_junction_curves checks that the mesh it is given lies inside the mask's extent (no coordinate below -1 or above the mask's size along its axis) and refuses otherwise, because a permuted axis order would put every curve tens of voxels away and the result would silently measure the permutation. The check sees only the extent: a mesh scaled down into it, or permuted on a mask whose sides are nearly equal, passes it.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: The detection, the MST-diameter spine and the endpoint-preserving three-point filter, the per-case reading spacing, the identity rule against the mesh's own trijunctions and the consistency test were developed and validated on the benchmark (BENCHMARKS.md, "Junction curves"). The sub-voxel estimator lives in junction_curve_estimator.

docs.text:
extract_junction_curves(segmented_mask: NDArray[uint], points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64], labels: NDArray[int64], *, estimator: Estimator = 'plain') -> JunctionCurves

Trijunction curves from the mask, keyed to the mesh's own trijunctions.

The one line a user writes::

curves = extract_junction_curves(mask, *load_rec("000_mesh.rec"))

curves.matched is the usable set. Every one of its members has exactly one counterpart among the mesh's own trijunctions of the same material triple, so it can be joined to the interfaces and the dihedral angles the reconstruction already reports. curves.invented is everything the mask says is a junction and the mesh does not have; 0 of 16 of those were measured within one voxel of all three of their interfaces, against a median of 0.68 voxels for the matched ones, so they are kept apart rather than merged. curves.fragmented holds real trijunctions the mask resolves as several pieces.

Reading spacing is not a parameter: the polylines are resampled at the mesh's own median trijunction-edge length, so accuracy is compared at the resolution the mesh states its lines at rather than at whatever resolution the lattice happens to give.

Cost, and why "plain" is the default. "plain" is detection only -- no linear program -- and costs about 0.8 s per benchmark case against the 1.49 s dw3d spends reconstructing that case. "anchor" solves one small linear program per returned vertex and costs roughly fifteen times as much, about eight times the whole reconstruction it annotates, and buys 9-11 % of the position error. Nobody meshing a large tissue should pay that by default, so they do not.

"anchor"'s real argument is not that 9 %: it is that the polytope's deepest interior point carries only the irreducible narrow-wedge term (a) of the mask's identifiability floor, where the detected position and the centroid both carry more. Reach for it when a systematic bias against narrow wedges would corrupt what you are inferring, not to shave a tenth of a voxel. "centroid" is kept for comparison only: it was measured carrying (a) + (b), so it is the larger systematic, not the smaller one, and it costs about thirty times the anchor's linear programs on top.

docs.title: Junction relocation
docs.text: Move a finished mesh's trijunction vertices onto the trijunction curves the mask itself gives.

docs.title: What it does, and what it deliberately does not
docs.text:
:func:relocate_junction_vertices changes points and never triangles or labels. The connectivity is frozen, which is the whole argument for this construction over earlier attempts to improve junction geometry in this package: those moved tessellation points and let the Delaunay re-bracket the junction line, so the line could move the wrong way when the bracket changed. Here there is no bracket to change, and the treated mesh can be hashed against its own base.

The target is read from the mask, through :func:dw3d.junction_curves.extract_junction_curves, and only its matched curves are used -- the ones with exactly one counterpart among the mesh's own trijunctions of the same material triple. invented curves are never used as targets; fragmented curves are left untouched. No ground truth enters at any point: nothing here reads a reference mesh, a tension, a pressure or a Neumann angle, and the whole path has been re-run from a directory holding only the label image with a bit-identical result.

docs.title: Two guards, and why both are needed
docs.text:
Local. Moves are applied one vertex at a time in ascending vertex index, against the configuration as it stands rather than against the original, so two neighbouring junction vertices cannot both be accepted on the strength of a geometry neither will end up in. A move is accepted only if every triangle incident to that vertex keeps its normal orientation and keeps its area above :data:MIN_TRIANGLE_AREA, and if it leaves no cell on either side of those triangles with a signed volume of zero or less (a cell that already had one before the pass is not constrained). A rejected move is dropped, never repaired: the vertex stays where it was.

The cell clause exists because the triangle clause is blind to it: on a real embryo timepoint a cell made of a single tetrahedron had one vertex moved 6.7 voxels across the opposite face, every incident triangle kept a normal within 49 degrees of its previous one, and the cell's volume went from +35 to -5.8 cubic voxels. Its surface stayed closed, oriented, manifold and free of crossings, so no other check in the package saw it. The clause tests only the sign, deliberately: a floor at a fraction of the cell's volume before relocation was tried and refused more, because for the small cells that need it that volume is itself wrong, and a refused move freezes a vertex shared by several cells.

Nonlocal. A local guard cannot certify a nonlocal property. A move can drive one sheet of the mesh through a distant sheet while every triangle incident to the moved vertex stays perfectly oriented; measured on this package's benchmark cohort, all twelve local validity predicates stayed bit-identical on 40 of 40 cases while 23 such crossings existed on 5 of them. The second guard closes that: moving one vertex v changes the geometry of exactly the triangles incident to v, so every non-adjacent triangle pair with neither member incident to v has the same status before and after. The change in the whole-mesh crossing count therefore equals the change restricted to the pairs with at least one member incident to v -- an exact identity, not a neighbourhood approximation, because those partners range over the entire mesh. Accepting a move only when that restricted change is non-positive makes the crossing count non-increasing along the accepted sequence by construction.

That argument is checked rather than trusted: with verify=True the whole-mesh certificate of :mod:dw3d.triangle_intersection runs before and after, both counts are reported, and a rise raises rather than being absorbed.

docs.title: What this costs, and what it buys
docs.text: Measured over 40 equilibrium benchmark cases at four reconstruction spacings and on four point samplers, 16 independent adjudications. What the pass costs is best stated in seconds, because the reconstruction it follows varies by an order of magnitude between volumes: on the benchmark meshes, whose reconstruction takes about 5 s, it adds about 0.75 s (+15 %); on real embryo volumes, whose reconstruction takes about 0.6 s, it adds 0.1 to 1.5 s per timepoint (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on the two measured time series, +27 % to +208 %). Within one real series it grows faster than linearly with the number of triangles -- a fitted exponent of 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range of mesh sizes in a fixed imaging volume, which describes that series and is not a tissue-scale law. About half of it is the nonlocal guard's candidate-pair search and a third the mask trijunction-curve extraction. The nonlocal guard refuses between 0.04 % and 0.21 % of the moves the local guard accepts, and that is enough to take the crossing count to zero everywhere. Line position error, local tangent error and discrete curvature all improve with their confidence intervals clear of zero at every spacing and on every sampler, and no pre-existing validity predicate changes on any case. On the seed-free samplers it also improves contact angles by 2.3 to 3.5 degrees and gauge-matched tension error by 20-40 %; on the seeded default sampler the line improves and the angle does not move significantly.

docs.title: Quadruple points
docs.text: A junction vertex lying on two or more matched trijunction lines has targets that disagree. The rule is to leave it where it is, and report how many there are. Nothing here invents a consensus position for such a vertex.

docs.title: Units and conventions
docs.text: All coordinates are mask voxel units -- the frame a reconstructed dw3d mesh's points live in and the frame :func:~dw3d.junction_curves.extract_junction_curves emits its polylines in. That extractor refuses a mesh whose coordinates do not lie inside the mask's extent, which catches most permuted axis orders; a mesh scaled down into the extent, or permuted on a mask whose sides are nearly equal, passes that check. Areas are square voxels. Vertex order, array shape and dtype are preserved exactly.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: A mesh with no matched curve is returned unchanged with n_targets = 0; that is reported, not raised. A matched curve of fewer than two vertices carries no segment and is skipped and counted. A vertex with no incident triangle is skipped. The thresholds here are fixed and are not tuning parameters; they must not be adjusted to improve a reported metric.

docs.title: CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Junction relocation ran at a point spacing where its effect on tangent-based angles is unverified.

Emitted by :meth:dw3d.reconstruction_algorithm.MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask once per reconstruction, when junction relocation is on (the default) and the point-placement function's min_distance is at least :data:COARSE_SPACING_MIN_DISTANCE. A placement function that carries no min_distance (a custom callable rather than one of the factory's functools.partial placements) never triggers it, because the spacing cannot be read.

What it means: at min_distance 5 the surface-tangent description of the contact angles moved by a small amount lying within the noise of the check that reads it, and no larger spacing has been measured. Facet-based contact angles improve at every spacing measured. The warning is a subclass of :class:UserWarning, so it can be silenced or promoted to an error on its own with :func:warnings.filterwarnings, and whether it fired is recorded in the algorithm's relocation_provenance. To reproduce the 0.4 behaviour, construct the algorithm with relocate_junctions=False or call set_junction_relocation(False) on the factory.

build_vertex_pair_sets(points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[integer], targets: dict[int, NDArray[float64]]) -> tuple[dict[int, NDArray[np.int64]], float]

For each vertex with a target, a superset of the pairs its move can change the status of.

The superset is built from the base centroids with an inflation that covers every displacement the pass can ever propose, so one static index serves the whole pass: a triangle's centroid moves by at most the largest displacement d of its own three vertices, its radius about that centroid grows by at most 2 d, and two triangles can meet only when their centroids lie within the sum of their radii. A pair that can ever meet therefore satisfies |c_f - c_t| <= r_f + r_t + 3 (d_f + d_t) at base. Writing reach = r + 3 d, the pairs of a vertex are every (f, t) with f incident to the vertex, t != f, |c_f - c_t| <= reach_f + reach_t (evaluated as np.linalg.norm of the centroid difference), and f and t sharing no vertex.

The neighbour search is one batched k-d tree search per pair of reach bins (:func:_neighbours_within_reach) rather than one ball query per triangle inflated by the mesh's largest reach; the exact criterion above then decides, so the pair sets are the same whatever the search proposes.

docs.title: Anisotropic masks
docs.text: Mask preprocessing before meshing: resampling a mask with anisotropic voxels to cubic voxels.

docs.title: Why this module exists
docs.text:
dw3d meshes a label image on its own voxel grid. When the voxels are longer along one axis (typically z) than along the other two, meshing on that grid and scaling the mesh afterwards samples the surfaces coarsely along the long axis: the junction triangles come out about k times taller (k = long spacing / short spacing) and their normals, hence every contact angle read from them, are off. Resampling the mask to cubic voxels by shape-based interpolation before meshing removes most of that error. Measured on masks down-sampled along z by k (each coarse voxel takes the label covering most of it), one meshing seed, as the median over cases of each mesh's median line-mean contact-angle error minus that of the same mask meshed at full resolution:

  • on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells voxelised at a real cell size: meshing the native grid costs +1.38 deg at k = 5/3, +1.97 at 2 and +4.10 at 3; resampling first, +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17;
  • on foambryo's benchmark, whose cells are larger (42 cases): native +1.43, +2.43 and +5.58 deg at k = 5/3, 2, 3; resampled +0.43, +1.54 and +1.27.

Tension errors follow. Repeating slices (nearest neighbour) is worse than shape-based interpolation at every anisotropy above 2, and coarsening the two short axes, or passing the anisotropy to the distance transform alone, is worse than not resampling at all. Nothing was measured above k = 3 at real cell size. foambryo's quadric angle reading, which helps on the benchmark's larger cells, made every route worse at real cell size: keep foambryo's default reading.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• spacing is the voxel size along the array's axes (axis 0, axis 1, axis 2), so (dz, dy, dx) for a (z, y, x) stack, in any one unit. Exactly one axis may be coarser than the other two, which must be equal (to a relative SPACING_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE); this is the case of a microscope stack with its z step larger than its pixel size. Other spacings raise.
  • Frame: the centre of voxel j along an axis lies at j * spacing along that axis, so the first voxel of the input and of the output share their centre, and the output covers exactly the input's span between its first and last voxel centres. The output spacing is the short spacing h on every axis.
  • The output has the input's dtype and labels; no label is created.

docs.text:
resample_to_isotropic(mask: NDArray, spacing: tuple[float, float, float], method: str = 'shape') -> NDArray

Resample a label mask with one coarse axis to cubic voxels of the short spacing.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask NDArray

3-D integer label image (0 = medium or background).

required spacing tuple[float, float, float]

voxel size along axes 0, 1, 2, so (dz, dy, dx) for a (z, y, x) stack (see the module's conventions).

required method str

"shape" (default) or "nearest", see RESAMPLING_METHODS.

'shape'

Returns:

Type Description NDArray

The resampled mask, same dtype, on cubic voxels of size isotropic_spacing(spacing). Along the coarse axis

NDArray

it has floor((n - 1) k) + 1 voxels for n input voxels. **When the voxels are already cubic the input

NDArray

array itself is returned**, unchanged and uncopied, so an isotropic mask goes through bitwise.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for an unknown method, a mask that is not 3-D, or an unsupported spacing.

The shape-based method (Raya & Udupa, 1990): for every label, including 0, its 2-D signed distance is computed on every input slice across the coarse axis (positive inside, zero half-way between voxel centres) and interpolated linearly between slice centres; each output voxel takes the label with the largest value, ties to the smaller label. Where a label is present in one slice and absent from the next, the absent slice's value is min(d - k, -1/2) (d the present slice's): the surface keeps closing at one voxel per voxel, but never reaches the centre of a slice where the mask says the label is absent. Known bias: linear interpolation of a concave distance profile underestimates it, so small convex cells shrink slightly (measured on balls of radius 9-14 voxels: -1 to -5 % of their volume at k = 3, -5 to -11 % at k = 4). Each label is computed only in its bounding box (SHAPE_INTERPOLATION_MARGIN), so the cost grows with the cells' volume, not with the number of labels times the volume: about 40 s and 23 GiB for a 1 866-cell tissue of 4.98e8 voxels at k = 5/3. The measurements behind the choice are summarised in the module docstring.

docs.title: Decoupling the surface vertex set from the tesselation point set
docs.text:
dw3d's extraction is primal: a mesh triangle is a face of the tetrahedralisation, so every mesh vertex is a seed point. The boundary layer exploits that the other way round — it adds offset points a distance delta into each adjacent material precisely so that near-interface tetrahedra stop having all four vertices on the interface, which it achieves spectacularly (all-surface tets 40 % -> 0.8 %). But the offsets are then surface vertices too, and they sit delta voxels off the surface by design.

Measurement showed what that costs: the offsets are 30-35 % of mesh vertices, carry epsilon_rms = 2.51 voxels against the other families' 0.58-0.60, and account for 90 % of epsilon^2 — where epsilon is the vertex-to-true-surface distance that sets the junction-angle error through the calibrated error = C * epsilon / ell, C = 33.2 +- 1.2 deg.

exclude_offsets_from_surface removes them from the surface while leaving the tesselation, the watershed and the labelling untouched: each offset is merged onto its parent — the interface sample it is a delta-displacement of, which lies on the interface — and the triangles that collapse as a result are dropped. The surface vertex set becomes a subset of the interface samples and junction samples, i.e. of the points that were placed on the geometry, and the tesselation keeps every point it needs.

Two measurements decided this construction over the more literal alternative (move the vertex to "the EDT zero-set" along a tet edge):

  • The EDT has no zero-set at the interface. compute_edt_classical builds a valley, not a signed distance: interface samples sit at EDT 0.0-1.24 (median 0.82) with the level set by the local boundary thickness, and cell interiors are distance + max(edt_2). The interface is a local minimum set, so "project to the zero level set" is ill-posed; the well-posed operation is a 1-D minimisation across the sheet.
  • Doing that minimisation lands each offset 0.026 voxel (median) from an interface sample that is already a mesh vertex. The offsets carry no independent surface geometry: they are duplicates of the samples they were displaced from. Projecting them therefore produced 1234 triangles under 1 deg of minimum angle, 92 of exactly zero area and 409 normal flips on 3.tif alone — while merging them is exact, needs no interpolation and no threshold.

Sacha Ichbiah 2021. Matthieu Perez 2024.

Extract a labeled mesh from a labeled tesselation graph.

Winding convention. Every returned triangle has labels[i, 0] < labels[i, 1], and its right-hand-rule normal (p1 - p0) x (p2 - p0) points out of the region labels[i, 0] and into the region labels[i, 1]. This is the convention foambryo's cell volumes rely on (+det to the first label, -det to the second, by the divergence theorem). A triangle on the tesselation's hull (a border triangle, whose one tetrahedron carries a cell label) has labels (0, cell), so its normal points into the cell, i.e. into the hull.
